steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Context: the social, cultural, historical and political circumstances in which a play was written AND in which it is performed. | Key Fact: Original context shapes the play's meaning — An Inspector Calls (1945, set 1912) uses dramatic irony about world wars the audience knew had happened. | Key Fact: Modern production context: a director may reset a play in a different period to make contemporary connections — this changes the meaning. | Key Fact: Social influences: class, gender, race, power structures — these are reflected in and critiqued by drama.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Why is it important to understand the social and historical context of a play when analysing it? | How might a modern production of a classic play change the meaning through its context? Give an example. | Explain how the original performance context of a play you have studied affects its meaning.
